Priya, it is a real cell, and it is doing exactly what it looks like. The dark
mass is a [microglial process]{.dfn}, a branch of a microglia cell, in the act
of [phagocytosis]{.dfn}, which is the cell eating something. Microglia are the
brain's resident immune cells. When a synapse is tagged for removal, a
microglial branch extends toward it, wraps around the target, and engulfs it.

![A microglial process (blue) wrapped around a dendritic spine. Three slices through the tissue and one 3D view of the same cell.](sample-figure.png)

## Why a cell would eat a synapse

This is called synaptic pruning. It is essential while the brain is developing,
and it continues at a lower rate in adults. The dark, dense look comes from the
digestive machinery inside the branch, which is breaking down what it swallowed.

::: {.spec}
[Speculation]{.lbl}[We think the spine had already been marked for removal before the microglia arrived, but nothing in this dataset can tell us that directly.]{.mark-inline}
:::

## How to find more

Look for dark, dense processes that wrap around the receiving side of a synapse.
They differ from astrocyte processes, which are thinner and more even in texture.
